question: Should the recovery-point, host-handoff, and restored-admission contract be accepted as a normative extension of RFC 0013, or should it be split into a separate draft RFC before review continues?
rationale: The branch defines a new cross-owner host lifecycle boundary, while RFC 0013 is presented as a completed one-database snapshot contract; repository policy requires maintainer acceptance for RFC direction and automation cannot choose that product boundary safely.

options.title: Create a separate draft RFC
options.body: Keep RFC 0013 as the completed SQLite artifact contract and review the lifecycle sidecars as a separately scoped draft linked to the scale-to-zero issue.

options.title: Accept as an RFC 0013 extension
options.body: Retain the sidecars under RFC 0013, but explicitly record that maintainers accept this expanded normative lifecycle scope and its host compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Create a separate draft RFC
recommendation.body: Keep RFC 0013 as the completed SQLite artifact contract and review the lifecycle sidecars as a separately scoped draft linked to the scale-to-zero issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposal identifies Vincent's snapshot and suspension-validation work as the principal foundation whose contract boundary this addendum extends.
